elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 states that nothing in Section 6 restricts the projects in which the Company may participate or the products it may offer, eliminating the operative non-compete previously imposed on the Company.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 expressly preserves the Company's freedom regarding products, projects, and use or licensing of the Deerskin brand, removing the prior Internet-site and direct-to-consumer field limitations.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited in subject matter to one expressly named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains: Section 6.1 affirmatively provides that Section 6 does not restrict the Company's products or projects. The condition requiring a product-specific limitation is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the term of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: No operative restriction remains during or after the term, so there is no restriction extending beyond the term.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: Because the revised clause imposes no restriction, no restricted period can exceed 12 months, notwithstanding the Agreement's automatic renewals.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for internal development.
elements.evidence: There is no restriction requiring a carve-out; moreover, the unrestricted right to participate in projects encompasses internal development.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: There is no operative restriction to apply to acquired products or businesses, so the condition requiring an acquisition carve-out is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline completely removes the Company's non-compete and field-of-use restrictions and replaces them with a concise affirmative statement of freedom regarding products, projects, and the Deerskin brand. The fallback is also satisfied because it imposes only limits on a restriction, and no restriction remains. The term provision and Section 6.2 are unchanged, and the revision introduces no contradiction in the supplied operative text.
